summary:
Kazakhstan decriminalised consensual sex between men in late 1997, when Article 104 of the Penal Code, which criminalised "buggery", was repealed; the repeal took effect in 1998 and introduced a common age of consent of 16. Sex between women was never a criminal offence. The sources record no statute regulating clothing by gender presentation and no law restricting which toilet or facility a trans visitor may use.

A statutory ban on "propaganda of non-traditional sexual orientation" is the operative legal threat. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the law on 30 December 2025, prohibiting "information containing propaganda of pedophilia and/or non-traditional sexual orientation" in public spaces and in the media, with violations punishable by a 10-day arrest and a fine. The Mäjilis had approved a harsher version on 12 November 2025. Kazakhstan now stands with Russia, Hungary and Georgia among jurisdictions that ban "LGBTQ propaganda" by statute. The measure grew out of a petition, "We Are against Open and Hidden LGBT Propaganda in Kazakhstan!", filed by the Union of Parents; in June 2024 the Ministry of Culture and Information said it was reviewing the petition after it met the threshold for government consideration, and Human Rights Watch warned that the proposed ban would violate rights nationwide.

No law protects LGBT people from discrimination in employment, education, housing, health care, public accommodations or credit, so a trans visitor refused service or dismissed from a placement has no statutory remedy. Public opinion is heavily adverse: 89 per cent of respondents opposed same-sex marriage in a 2015-16 Pew survey.

Bias-motivated violence goes largely unrecorded by the state. Kazakhstan has not reported hate-crime data to the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights since the 2018 reporting cycle and has no nominated national point of contact for hate crimes; the OSCE assessment notes the country would benefit from victim-support and awareness measures.

Documented incidents set the pattern. During 2023 an LGBTQI activist was almost run over by a car in an apparent deliberate attack that produced no investigation, and an LGBTQI+ education organisation was refused registration as an employment site after disclosing its focus, according to ILGA-Europe's review of access to services. In 2019 the Supreme Court upheld a privacy claim against a Facebook user who posted a video of two women kissing and solicited homophobic comments, ordering compensation over a "moral foundations" defence; the two women left Kazakhstan for eight months fearing for their safety.

Barriers to health care for LGBT people are documented by the Eurasian Coalition on Male Health, which has recorded rights violations in the country since 2017 and reports that informal behavioural practices shaping access are missed by formal policy analysis.

Partner recognition is absent. Kazakhstan does not recognise same-sex marriage or civil unions, and households headed by same-sex couples receive none of the legal protections available to married opposite-sex couples. A trans visitor travelling with a partner in a relationship that would be read as same-sex under local birth-sex status should expect no spousal recognition, no next-of-kin standing and no protection tied to the relationship.
tangentialFactors:
Since 2022 transgender people have continued to arrive in Kazakhstan from Russia, a movement driven by legal conditions in the neighbouring jurisdiction; the demand it places on services and community infrastructure is the adjacent regional pressure on the country's trans population.

The 2025 propaganda law aligns Kazakhstan with other jurisdictions in the region holding comparable statutory bans, among them Russia, Hungary and Georgia. Independent media described the February 2024 adoption restriction as modelled on Russian legislation.
localsOnly:
Legal gender recognition has been available on identity documents since 2003, but only through a diagnosis of "gender identity disorder". Applicants undergo medical tests and a 30-day psychiatric evaluation by a medical commission, and pay a fee of around 100,000 tenge.

Since 2011 changes to documents have required gender-affirming surgery, hormone therapy and sterilisation, and no one under 21 may change gender on documents at all. Although commissions may in principle be assembled in every region since 2023, the only functioning one in practice is in Almaty, because of requirements for separate specialist rooms. A positive decision yields a certificate valid for six months in which to begin medical transition.

Same-sex couples have been unable to adopt children legally since at least 2020, and in February 2024 President Tokayev signed a law prohibiting adoption of orphans by same-sex couples. Deputy Minister of Education Natalya Jumadildaeva stated that a prospective parent's sexual orientation would play a "key role" in approval, assessed through a "special psychological test".
outOfScopeNotes:
The propaganda law's penalties are stated in statute as a 10-day administrative arrest and a fine. Whether the measure has been applied to individuals, and to whom, is not established by the sources, and no case counts or enforcement records are available.

The country's last hate-crime submission to the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights covers the 2018 reporting cycle, and no national point of contact for hate crimes is nominated. The scale of anti-trans violence is therefore unquantified; no official or independent figure is sourced.

The 2023 refusal to register an LGBTQI+ education organisation as an employment site is recorded without a resolution or appeal outcome. In the 2019 case, the Supreme Court ordered compensation, but the amount awarded and whether the video was taken down are not sourced.

How the medical-commission requirements for legal gender recognition apply to foreign nationals or visitors is unresolved; the sources describe the process only for residents. The Pew finding on opposition to same-sex marriage dates from 2015-16, and no more recent national polling is sourced.
